# File

<!-- gen:begin summary -->
<!-- Generated by `npm run generate:op-docs` from noodles-validate/registry.json. The title and the text between gen:begin and gen:end markers are replaced on every run; write anywhere else. -->

Fetch a file from a URL or text. Supports csv, tsv, json, text, and binary formats.
<!-- gen:end summary -->

## Syntax

<!-- gen:begin syntax -->
```json
{
  "id": "/file",
  "type": "FileOp",
  "position": { "x": 0, "y": 0 },
  "data": { "inputs": {} }
}
```

Expressions and code read its fields as `op('/file').par.format` (an input) and `op('/file').out.data` (an output). Edges name the same fields as handles: `par.format`, `out.data`.
<!-- gen:end syntax -->

## Inputs

<!-- gen:begin inputs -->
| Name | Type | Default |
|------|------|---------|
| `format` | `StringLiteralField` | `"json"` |
| `url` | `FileUrlField` | `""` |
| `text` | `StringField` | `""` |
| `autoType` | `BooleanField` | `true` |
| `pulse` | `NumberField` | `0` |
<!-- gen:end inputs -->

## Outputs

<!-- gen:begin outputs -->
| Name | Type |
|------|------|
| `data` | `DataField` |
<!-- gen:end outputs -->

## Remarks

File loads one file and outputs its parsed contents as `data`. When `url` is set, `text` is ignored. With neither set, the output is an empty value in the format's shape: `{}` for json, `[]` for csv and tsv, `''` for text and an empty byte array for binary, so downstream operators run instead of failing.

A `url` that starts with `@/` reads a file stored with the project, so `@/data.csv` is the `data.csv` in the project's folder, beside `noodles.json`. That needs a loaded project: in a new, unsaved project it fails with "No project loaded". Any other URL is fetched by the browser, so a server on another domain has to allow cross-origin requests (CORS).

For json, text and binary, File uses the response whatever its HTTP status. A JSON error body from an API arrives as `data` as if it were the file, and a 404 page fails to parse as JSON. csv and tsv fail on any non-OK status. When a json source looks wrong, open the URL in a browser tab to see what the server sent.

`autoType` appears only for csv and tsv. It runs every row through [d3.autoType](https://d3js.org/d3-dsv#autoType): number-like strings become numbers, `true` and `false` become booleans, ISO 8601 dates become `Date` objects and empty cells become `null`. That's what you want for sizing and coloring by a column, but it also strips leading zeros, so a ZIP code like `02134` becomes `2134`. Turn `autoType` off to keep every value a string and convert the columns you need downstream.

`pulse` is never read. Changing any input runs the operator again, so changing `pulse`, by hand or from a connected number, fetches the same URL again, for example to pick up a file that changes on the server. The browser's HTTP cache still applies to that request.

## Examples

A CSV stored with the project, with `autoType` off so ID columns keep their leading zeros:

```json
{ "id": "/stations", "type": "FileOp", "position": { "x": 0, "y": 0 }, "data": { "inputs": { "format": "csv", "url": "@/stations.csv", "autoType": false } } }
```

A few rows typed into `text`, for a quick test without a file:

```json
{ "id": "/test-points", "type": "FileOp", "position": { "x": 0, "y": 0 }, "data": { "inputs": { "format": "json", "text": "[{\"lng\": -122.42, \"lat\": 37.77}, {\"lng\": -73.99, \"lat\": 40.73}]" } } }
```
